problems.description: 33 naming-convention violations (Functions/Classes/Interfaces camelCase|PascalCase, Constants UPPER_CASE), all concentrated in the new test files (cli.test.ts, frontmatter.test.ts), matching the mechanical convention score of 0.54.
SonarQube delta shows +19.5% duplications and +28 cognitive complexity added in a greenfield session — a meaningful amount of copied/repeated logic for 1126 new lines.

Session 1 deletes the entire 200-line seed baseline (index.ts) and replaces it with an unrelated domain (JWT auth API → static site generator), which is acceptable only because the story is 'greenfield'; otherwise this would be baseline destruction with no migration path.
package.json name/description ('ssg' / 'Static site generator CLI') contradicts the deleted seed's domain, signaling task/goal drift between the provided baseline and what the agent chose to build.

strengths: Replaces the 200-line monolith with a modular src/ tree (+11 functions, +15 files) — a genuine architectural improvement toward separation of concerns
Establishes a coherent test infrastructure: jest + ts-jest config whose roots/testMatch align with the actual src/__tests__/ layout, plus build/start/test/clean scripts and a bin entry
Zero new bugs or code smells per SonarQube, and no security regressions in the new dependencies (marked, gray-matter)
commit_reviews.summary: The commit restructures the seed into a cleaner modular, tested TypeScript project with no new bugs, but lands a low convention score (0.54) from 33 test-file naming violations and adds noticeable duplication.

compounding_issues: Session limit exhaustion: sessions 3, 4, and 5 each produced zero output (0 tokens, 0 cost) — their commits contain only a 3-line '.instrument/session_N.jsonl' placeholder reading 'You've hit your session limit', so the integration/refactor/cross_cutting phases never happened

Session 2 was cut off mid-refactor: the agent converted build() to async (src/ssg.ts:95) and 'marked' to await (src/ssg.ts:52), but only 3 of 26 test cases in src/__tests__/ssg.test.ts were updated to async/await — the remaining 23 call the now-async build() without awaiting, so the test suite is broken at the final commit

The async-conversion scope balloon: converting the build pipeline to async forced a rewrite of the entire test suite mid-session, which is what ran the session out of budget before it could finish or run the tests

Zero verification throughout: Node.js was unavailable in the agent environment ('TESTS: Unable to execute in current environment'), so all 41+ tests were written but never executed, and the broken async state was never caught
Unused declared dependency: gray-matter is listed in package.json but never imported — the agent hand-rolled its own YAML frontmatter parser in src/frontmatter.ts instead
The story runner scheduled 5 sessions across the daily session-limit reset boundary (2:10am), so 3 of the 5 sessions were starved of budget before starting
key_decisions: Session 1 chose to hand-write a custom YAML frontmatter parser and string-interpolated HTML templates in ssg.ts rather than using the already-declared gray-matter dependency — self-contained but duplicated work
Session 1 established a clean modular core (cli.ts / frontmatter.ts / ssg.ts / index.ts) with extensive jest coverage and docs — the strongest decision of the story

Session 2 adopted Handlebars with a templates/{layouts,partials}/ directory convention, per-page template/layout frontmatter fields, and default-fallback templates — a forward-looking, backwards-compatible architecture
Session 2 refactored the build pipeline to async (async marked + Promise.all across pages) — architecturally reasonable but it destabilized the test suite and was never completed
Dependency stack locked in as marked ^12 + gray-matter + handlebars under TypeScript/Jest ESM
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality started high and then collapsed: Session 1 (greenfield) delivered a complete, coherent SSG — clean module split, 41 tests, docs, working CLI. Session 2 (feature_addition) began sensibly by adding a Handlebars template/layout/partials engine with default fallbacks, but the agent decided to convert the build pipeline to async mid-session and hit its session limit partway through rewriting the test suite, committing a tree where 23 of 26 ssg.test.ts cases don't await the now-async build — i.e., a broken state. Sessions 3, 4, and 5 (integration, refactor, cross_cutting) each hit the session limit immediately and contributed zero code, zero tokens, and zero cost. The arc is therefore a strong start, a sharp mid-story breakage, and a flatline of no further work; the final commit is less functional than the session-1 baseline.
story_review.summary: Only sessions 1 and 2 did any real work, session 2 was abandoned mid-async-refactor leaving the test suite broken, and sessions 3-5 produced nothing (session-limit exhaustion), so the nominal 5-session progression is effectively 1.5 sessions ending in a non-green state.
